question:
Which approach is better for spacing between elements and why?
```css
.parent > .child { margin: 20px; } /* option A */
.parent { padding: 20px; } /* option B */
.parent { gap: 20px; } /* option C (if flex/grid) */
```
options: B: padding creates internal breathing room
C: gap only applies to flex/grid children
explanation: gap (flex/grid) avoids margin-collapse issues and double-spacing on edges; it's the modern approach for spacing children uniformly.
With content-box: width (100px) + padding (15px both sides = 30px) + border (5px both sides = 10px) = 140px rendered; margin is outside, so 140px + 20px margin = ignored in width.

options: Width 100% fills container, no room to center
margin: auto only works with position: absolute
explanation: margin: auto centers by using leftover space; width: 100% consumes all available space, leaving zero space to center.
Padding percentages always calculate relative to the element's width, not height, even for padding-top/bottom.
Floated elements don't participate in margin collapse; adjacent float margins add together (10px + 20px = 30px gap).
With box-sizing: content-box (default), height applies to content only; padding extends beyond, making total rendered height 140px, but overflow: hidden clips at 100px from the padding edge inward.
